text:
Shea Theodore's season is a puzzle. With him on the ice at 5v5, Vegas has 58.2% of the expected goals (the share of chance quality), a strong number for a defenseman playing 22.2 minutes a night. Yet he has 2 goals and 7 points in 25 games, and just two assists in his last ten against 3.9 expected points.

Our numbers lean toward bad luck. The Golden Knights have scored 6.0 fewer goals than the chances deserve with him on the ice, his own shooting (4.7%) sits below a talent range centred on 6.5%, and our talent range puts his scoring rate near 1.22 points per 60, well above the 0.76 he's at.

The cost has been real, though. Our wins-added measure, which credits goals by how much they swing a game, ranks him 541st of 559 skaters: his chances in big moments haven't gone in.

The defending holds up. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him stopping 15% of the entries aimed at him last season (typical is 11%), and Evolving-Hockey ranked him 46th among 215 defensemen at 1.5 wins above replacement.
